reasoning: A hybrid approach combines autonomous reasoning to identify initial patterns in shared feature values with external XAI tools to quantify feature attribution and detect spurious correlations. This ensures both domain-aware insights and statistically grounded attribution scores, improving the reliability of detecting spurious features that are present across misclassified instances but semantically unrelated to class labels.

autonomous_tasks.query: Compare the values of each feature across instances 537, 340, and 73 to identify which features have identical or highly similar values across all three misclassified samples.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features with shared or near-identical values across all three instances

autonomous_tasks.query: Evaluate whether any of the shared features (e.g., mean radius, texture) are semantically plausible as indicators of malignancy or benignancy based on medical domain knowledge.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features identified as semantically irrelevant or misleading for diagnosis

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP identifies global feature importance, helping detect spurious features with high impact despite lack of semantic relevance. LIME provides local interpretability for each instance, revealing how features contribute per case. Integrated Gradients offer gradient-based attribution, sensitive to model internals, while sensitivity analysis measures feature impact through ablation, confirming spuriousness by showing prediction instability when the feature is removed. Together, they validate shared spurious patterns across misclassified instances.
